newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmaker to boost coastal bond to $660 mln.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmaker to boost coastal bond to $660 mln.

text.p: A California state lawmaker plans to boost a proposed bond measure to $660 million to fund programs protecting the state's picturesque coastline, his office said on Friday.

Before its scheduled May 14 hearing in the appropriations committee, the bill's author, Assemblyman Fred Keeley, plans to increase the bond measure's size to approximately $660 million from $613 million, his office said.
"It's a bipartisan effort and there's absolutely no registered opposition," David Bunn, Keeley's legislative director, said.
Assembly Bill 1000 would enact the Clean Coastal Waters and Rivers Bond Act of 1998 to fight pollution to coastal waters and rivers.
If the bill is approved by the legislature, the general obligation bond measure would appear on the state ballot in November 1998.
Supporters of the measure contend that the bond funds are needed to protect the state's wildlife as well as the California economy.
These coastal areas generate more than $17 billion a year in economic activity, according to a report by the Assembly Committee on Natural Resources.
For decades, California has funded programs to protect its natural resources, including its coastline, by issuing bonds.
Since 1964, state voters have approved nine bond measures totaling $2.356 billion for the protection of parks, recreation and wildlife, the Assembly committee said.
The last successful bond act to allocate money to the coast was the California Wildlife, Coastal and Park Conservation Act in 1988, which generated $776 million.
But nearly all of that money has been spent, and what remains has been earmarked for specific projects, state officials said.
Keeley's office said the proposed Clean Coastal Waters and Rivers Bond Act of 1998 would provide approximately:
* $355 million to the State Coastal Conservancy to fund the acquisition, development, restoration and protection of coastal lands.
* $110 million to the Wildlife Conservation Board to fund programs to benefit fish and wildlife.
* $75 million to the River Protection and Enhancement Account for acquisition and restoration of land near rivers.
* $120 million to the Pollution Prevention Account to fund runoff and storm water pollution prevention programs and to purchase water quality monitoring equipment.
